quote: What direction should we choose as a people and as a human community?
Thirdly, building a world in which everyone can flourish requires shared responsibility and courage.
And yet we must remember that humanity flourishes not despite limitations, but often through them.
We must be faithful to the truth, invest in education, cultivate relationships and love justice and peace.
Let us love justice and peace!
In international relations, dialogue is an irreplaceable diplomatic tool for preventing conflicts and rebuilding bonds of trust.
Technology should not be considered, in itself, as a force antagonistic to humanity.
…we refer to moral dignity, namely the way in which a person directs his or her choices and actions.
To disarm does not mean rejecting technology, but preventing it from dominating humanity.
…humanity — in all its grandeur and woundedness — must never be replaced or surpassed.
All of us, at every level, can contribute to building the foundation of peace, which is justice.
In the abstract, technology in and of itself is not a solution to humanity’s problems, just as it is not inherently evil.
Even when these tools are described as capable of “learning,” their way of doing so is different from that of a human person.
To speak of solidarity obliges us to recognize the hidden, often exploited workers, who sustain algorithmic systems.
Even when limitations are experienced as inner suffering, human wisdom teaches us not to deny or suppress it, but to integrate it.
Even when machines excel in efficiency, a human face that asks to be gazed upon remains the center of our history.
Yet every era also runs the risk of creating an inhumane and more unjust world.
The value of persons, however, does not depend on what they achieve or produce.
When we speak of dignity, we do not always use the word in the same way.
We can describe it as the social expression of the dignity recognized in every person.
In this day and age, social justice must… grapple with the environment shaped by digital technologies.
For individuals as well as for nations, development is both a duty and a right.
When words are simulated, they do not build genuine relationships, but only their appearance.
The principles of Social Doctrine offer a framework for understanding this new reality.
…technological innovation can represent human participation in the divine act of creation.
To eliminate suffering entirely would mean, in the end, extinguishing love and desire as well.
When languages and tools change, so do everyday actions and social relationships.
…work is not simply an instrument; it expresses and enhances the dignity of our lives.
For young people, job insecurity is particularly devastating.
…freedom in the digital age is not merely a matter of interiority but also a public concern.
If we focus only on contingencies, we risk letting the succession of emergencies dictate the direction of our path.
…true fulfilment is not achieved by eliminating weakness but through harmonious growth…
…ours is the pressing duty to remain profoundly human…
Human dignity does not depend on a person’s abilities, wealth or position in life…
The fundamental dignity of each person… is neither acquired nor earned, nor does it need to be justified.
Human rights are inviolable, since they are “inherent in the human person and in human dignity.”
More power does not necessarily imply something better.
The quality of a civilization is measured not by the power of its means, but by the care it is able to offer…
The ability to care for one another is a fundamental dimension of our humanity…
Moral progress almost always unfolds through a long and demanding journey, often marked by setbacks.
…goodness does not advance automatically, but requires the perseverance, memory and interior conversion necessary to begin anew…
A society is noble and decent, not least for its support of the pursuit of truth and its adherence to the most basic of truths.
Indifference to the truth leads, slowly but surely, to a descent into totalitarianism.
The search for truth is an essential element of democracy, which is itself a means of contributing to the common good.
…innovation can serve as an ally of safer, more creative and dignified work…
Finance for its own sake is fundamentally different from finance aimed at the development, creation and evolution of work.
Today, justice requires access to the benefits of innovation, including care, knowledge, tools and opportunities.
The family is a primary social good.
Human trafficking must be recognized as a contemporary form of slavery and a grave violation of human dignity.
What we have learned must be translated into discernment and responsibility in the present.
We live at a time of significant spiritual and cultural blindness.
We do not consider the present as a predetermined fate, but an opportunity for personal and collective conversion.
Peace begins with each one of us: in the way we look at others, listen to others and speak about others.
Painful events require both history and memory, the former to recount the facts, the latter to bear witness to lived experiences.
Authentic realism does not give up on changing the world…
Those who make history are the peacemakers, not those who sow seeds of suffering.
Let us invest in education, beginning with ourselves!
…the human heart retains an irrevocable need for genuine closeness…
Quo vadis, humanitas?
